scenario: Kill the operator after all five agents accept a 2 m north mission; verify each agent independently lands and disarms after its mission lease expires.

measurement_method.completion_time: Harness wall time from operator process termination until all five fresh current statuses explicitly report command=landed, armed=false, airborne=false, and ground altitude.
measurement_method.separation: Across airborne agent_status records in events.jsonl, compare each position to each other vehicle's nearest event timestamp when the samples differ by at most 0.4 seconds; report the minimum horizontal N/E distance. This is sampled evidence, not a continuous collision bound.

excluded_or_inconclusive_evidence.reason: The legacy summary says all_landed but has no all_disarmed confirmation; its latest recorded statuses show all five still armed near ground with command=landing:mission_expired. Excluded from the five strict successes.
Seed-90 regression: the staggered-takeoff peer watchdog caused premature landing and the mission did not complete. Retained as a failed trial.
The earlier seed-50 observer did not record armed state, so it proves reaching ground but not disarm.

limitations: Five seeds validate this scenario on one host; they do not establish broad reliability or real-network behavior.
The minimum separation is based on timestamp-matched telemetry samples and can miss motion between samples.
This scenario demonstrates lease-expiry LAND after operator loss, not distributed consensus or physical-flight safety.
